name: The Bahamas
summary: From a depopulated archipelago to pirate havens, crown colony and independence.
notes: Nassau’s pirate ascendancy and brief U.S. raids did not constitute sovereignty over every Bahamian island. The contested interval records the collapse of colonial administration around Nassau.

events.title: Columbus lands in the Bahamas
events.detail: The Spanish claim began at Guanahaní, conventionally identified as San Salvador.
events.uncertainty: The precise modern identification of Guanahaní remains debated.

events.title: Enslavement devastates the Lucayans
events.detail: Spanish slaving expeditions removed the Indigenous population; no lasting Spanish colony followed.
events.uncertainty: An approximate marker for a gradual process, not a dated island-wide handover.

events.title: The Eleutheran Adventurers
events.detail: English settlers from Bermuda established a colony on Eleuthera.
events.uncertainty: Some histories use 1647 or 1649; 1648 is the conventional settlement date.

events.title: Nassau becomes a pirate haven
events.detail: Attacks and administrative collapse left Nassau dominated by pirates, while Britain retained its claim.

events.title: Royal government reasserted
events.detail: Woodes Rogers arrived to establish effective crown government.

events.title: American raid on Nassau
events.detail: Continental forces briefly seized forts and military supplies; this was not an archipelago-wide transfer.

events.title: Spain takes the Bahamas
events.detail: An expedition from Cuba compelled the British governor to surrender.

events.title: British rule returns
events.detail: Loyalist forces retook Nassau; the peace settlement confirmed British possession.

events.title: Bahamian independence
events.detail: The Commonwealth of The Bahamas became sovereign.
